governing: blueprint #authority: information ownership table, identifier link table, minimal relationship contract and outcomeId rule
principles: Each source record keeps its native ID; a reference never mints a new ID where a native one exists (blueprint #authority).
Other systems carry references and projections, not competing lifecycle states: a resolution reports what the authority shows and never a status of its own.
Historical links include the source revision so the Owner can reconstruct what was known when a decision was made: every kind states how a reference pins an immutable revision.
If a source relationship was never recorded, report missing provenance; never invent it. A resolution is never a silent success.

grammar.reference: <scheme>:<body>, where <scheme> is lower case and selects the kind (canonical_form of each kind gives the body)
grammar.segment: a native ID that the authority assigns and this schema does not constrain: its UTF-8 bytes, with every byte outside A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~ percent-encoded as %XX with upper-case hex digits; any other spelling is refused, so text and value correspond one to one
grammar.commit: a full git commit id: 40 lower-case hex digits, or 64 in a SHA-256 repository; never a branch, tag or abbreviation
grammar.repository: a repository name as its hosting authority names it: parts of [A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]* separated by /; Gitea kinds take exactly owner/name
grammar.canonical: every accepted text is canonical: format(parse(text)) == text and parse(format(reference)) == reference
grammar.intent_record: every kind's canonical form except design satisfies intent-record/v1's reference value grammar ^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:[^\s=,]+$ (catalog/skills/intent-normalization/references/intent-record.md), so it can be cited as an intent record's source, acceptance or resolution; the design pointer keeps the P-02.1 form, whose '=' that grammar refuses

outcomes.resolved: the authority answered, the identity exists and every anchor the reference pins matches; observed_revision and observed_digest report what it showed
outcomes.missing: the authority answered and does not hold the identity (at the pinned revision, when pinned): missing provenance, reported, never invented
outcomes.revision-mismatch: the authority does not hold the revision the reference pins (for example a commit lost to a history rewrite, or a journal event absent after a restore)
outcomes.digest-mismatch: the pinned revision exists but its content does not have the pinned digest
outcomes.authority-unavailable: the authority could not be asked: it does not exist yet, is not configured, refused access, failed or did not verify its own integrity; nothing is known about the reference
outcomes.unsupported-kind: the kind's identity is not settled, or no kind uses the scheme: the reference cannot be resolved by anything
outcomes.ambiguous: the identity matches more than one record in the authority

authority.name: Owner conversation store
authority.system_of_record: Owner conversation store: local conversation persistence behind assistant-ui
authority.blueprint: #authority, 'Original general conversation | Local conversation persistence behind assistant-ui | Stable thread and message reference'; #integration-contracts, 'General chat needs a small local durable thread store because ExternalStoreRuntime does not supply its own history database'

identity.native_id: the thread id the Owner conversation store assigns (a segment)

revision.anchor: @<message>: the thread as it stood through that message (the branch of the thread that ends at it)

kinds.validation_rule: Resolve a durable message or explicitly report missing source. (#authority, link 'Original statement')
open: Whether a message id names immutable content, and how an edit branches a thread, are U-02.1's edit semantics; the message kind's content digest is what pins bytes.

authority.name: Owner conversation store
authority.system_of_record: Owner conversation store: local conversation persistence behind assistant-ui
authority.blueprint: #authority, 'Original general conversation | Local conversation persistence behind assistant-ui | Stable thread and message reference'; link 'Original statement', notation conversation:thread-42/message-8

identity.native_id: the thread id and the message id the Owner conversation store assigns (two segments)

revision.anchor: #sha256:<hex>: the sha256 of the message content; or the span anchor #span:<start>+<length>:sha256:<hex>
revision.content: the message content is its text as UTF-8 bytes exactly as the durable store returns it: no Unicode normalisation, no newline conversion, no trimming

span_anchor.start: byte offset into the content, an integer >= 0 in canonical decimal
span_anchor.length: byte length, an integer >= 1 in canonical decimal
span_anchor.sha256: the sha256 of exactly content[start : start + length]; required whenever a span is given
span_anchor.boundaries: start and start + length fall on UTF-8 character boundaries and within the content
span_anchor.re_extraction: the quote is content[start : start + length] read from the durable source; it is verified when its sha256 equals the anchor's, byte for byte (Overseer ruling D2, evidence/P-01.2-intent-skill-qualification.md: a U+00A0 did not survive the model channel, so quotes are filled mechanically from the durable source and the model references spans)

kinds.validation_rule: Resolve a durable message or explicitly report missing source (#authority). With a digest: the content's sha256 equals it. With a span: the span lies within the content on character boundaries and its bytes' sha256 equals the anchor's; otherwise digest-mismatch. Implemented as lineage.check_message_content, ready for the U-02.1 store.
open: Which parts of a multi-part assistant-ui message form its content bytes, and how they are joined, is U-02.1's to define; the P-01.2 corpus message text stands in until then.

identity.native_id: the outcome id, minted when an Objective item's acceptance is recorded; a random UUID in canonical lower-case text, declared in the declaring change's .openspec.yaml under x-outcomes as {item: O<n>, acceptance: <reference>} (decision 0008)

revision.anchor: @<commit>: the project repository commit at which the declaring change is read; observed_digest is the sha256 of the declaring change's proposal.md blob at that commit

kinds.validation_rule: From git objects only, at the pinned commit or at HEAD for current: enumerate openspec/changes/<change>/.openspec.yaml and openspec/changes/archive/<dated-change>/.openspec.yaml; exactly one declares the id, else missing or ambiguous; the declared item exists in that change's proposal Objective section with authority: accepted and the same acceptance, else the outcome does not resolve; a resolved answer reports the declaring change, the item, its acceptance, its source and the accepted Acceptance Criteria that cite it (decision 0008, point 6). Trace to source statement, acceptance conditions and current revision. (#authority, link 'Accepted objective')
kinds.resolver: lineage_resolve.ObjectiveResolver (the P-02.1 git reader and the intent-record/v1 parser)

outcome_codes.missing: OUTCOME_MISSING; OUTCOME_NOT_ACCEPTED (declared item absent, not an Objective item, not accepted, or its acceptance differs)
outcome_codes.authority-unavailable: PROJECT_UNAVAILABLE, GIT_FAILED, OUTCOME_METADATA_INVALID (x-outcomes or the intent record unreadable)

kinds.verified: offline: throwaway git repositories (integrations/lineage/tests); live: openspec validate --strict and openspec archive with OpenSpec 1.16.0 when AIEH_OPENSPEC is set
citations: blueprint #authority (outcomeId rule; the link notation outcome:O-101 is illustrative)
blueprint #integration-contracts ('OpenSpec goal and x-fields'; 'We own stable IDs')
OpenSpec docs/cli.md at v1.16.0 (x- keys are the user's own; archive moves a change to openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/)
evidence/P-01.2-intent-skill-qualification.md (the accepted objective recorded as O1 with acceptance conversation:qual-02/message-2)
open: The acceptance recorder (sets the item's authority and acceptance, mints the id, writes the declaration, commits) has no owning plan leaf; until it exists, Owner acceptances are recorded by hand in this form (decision 0008, Consequences).
Supersession links between outcomes are not defined (K-03.3.2).
Acceptance references of scheme decision: have no lineage kind; one is added when a traversal needs it.

revision.anchor: @<commit>: a full commit id of the repository that holds Backlog.md's files; the task is read by Backlog.md itself (task view --json) from an export of that commit, never by reading its markdown

kinds.validation_rule: Query supported Backlog API; don't assume Work is done because an agent finished. (#authority, link 'Work') Only task view --json and task list --json are run; no status is read for a verdict or reported.

kinds.verified: offline with the fake Backlog.md and the recorded P-02 fixtures; live against Backlog.md 1.55.3 when AIEH_BACKLOG and AIEH_OPENSPEC are set
open: The Backlog.md task has no content digest anchor: its JSON output is the tool's, not an immutable record, so a digest-mismatch cannot arise for this kind.
Backlog.md 1.55.3 refuses task list --json when two tasks share an id (P-02.2); the resolver then answers authority-unavailable with Backlog.md's message, not ambiguous.

revision.anchor: @<seq>#sha256:<hash>: one journal event of this receipt (its sequence number) and that event's hash-chain value, sha256(prev_hash || LF || content); the receipt as of that event

kinds.validation_rule: The journal must verify (verify_chain) before any answer. A restore loses knowledge, never effects: the absence of a receipt after a restore is not evidence that an effect did not happen (decision 0004, point 7), so missing says only that the store holds no receipt.
kinds.resolver: lineage_resolve.EffectReceiptResolver (EffectsStore.get, events, verify_chain; read methods only)
kinds.verified: offline on F-05.2 fixture stores only; no live effects store exists (decision 0004, point 4)
open: On the live store, OS custody denies ordinary integration processes (decision 0004, point 1): a resolver not run under the store's custody identity answers authority-unavailable. Live resolution belongs with G-04.2.1 and G-04.2.2.
open_effects_store, the store's only open path, applies pending migrations in a write transaction; at the current schema it changes no content (tested), but the store has no strictly read-only open.
